A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Statistical Deficiency for Task Inclusion Estimation. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison, including matching material across layout shifts.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on HMM-generated tasks and OntoNotes NLP tasks, including model scores, information-sufficiency measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original synthetic and NLP experiments and their results, including the supplementary comparisons and layer ablations.

M1.justification: The embedding-based task-comparison procedure, KNIFE information-sufficiency estimator, layer selection, and predictive-power calculation are retained. Added notation explanations do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three HMM-generated classification tasks and five OntoNotes-based NLP tasks: SYN, SRL, NER, COR, and SUM. Languages, domains, and evaluated scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Appendix F.3 retains the naive cross-task comparisons using BERTScore and ROUGE. Appendix H retains the cosine, L2, and Grassmann task-vector comparisons, with unchanged comparator membership.

E3.justification: Both retain the 1297/98/97 document splits, Mistral 7B and Llama 3 8B configurations, rank-8 LoRA, six training epochs, and layers 10–15 for the principal analysis. Appendix D's training and estimator settings also match.

E4.justification: The layer-selection analysis, alternative layer-range ablations, naive cross-evaluation correlations, and task-vector analyses in Appendices F–H are retained. Relocated displays do not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain averaging over 11 synthetic datasets, Table 7's parenthesized statistics, and the plotted uncertainty bands. Footnote 12's caveat about aggregate confidence intervals remains; no new run counts, seeds, or statistical procedures are reported.

E6.justification: The reported scores, rankings, correlations, and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains IS(F→F)=0.736, and Table 9 retains Llama 3 base correlations of 0.02 for BERTScore and 0.43 for ROUGE.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorems, and derivations in Section 3 and Appendices A–C and H are retained. The new Appendix B.1 footnote identifying skills with the conditional measure repeats an existing interpretation rather than adding mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a task-inclusion framework, a tractable information-sufficiency proxy, and empirical recovery of the NLP pipeline. Minor wording edits do not change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: Section 4 replaces the statement that NER and COR are not essential for SYN or SRL with a more nuanced account of NER's interdependence with SYN/SRL, explaining assistance in both directions. The principal result interpretations and stated limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a linked statement on page 1 that code and data are available; v1 only promises future availability of the generated dataset. Implementation details and hyperparameters otherwise match.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Section 2 retains the same relationships to task similarity, merging, transfer, and probing; the reference lists match after formatting normalization.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliations and contact wording and makes limited prose, terminology, and notation clarifications, including the Appendix B.1 footnote. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All 14 figures and 12 tables remain. Appendix figures and tables are repositioned, sometimes separating explanatory text across pages, while Figures 13–14 correct SEM labels to SRL. Display designs and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility documentation through explicit code/data access information and clarifies NER's relationship to SYN/SRL while correcting inconsistent figure labels. These provide modest gains despite some less convenient appendix pagination. The method, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
